flags: WATERFRONT: stored 'lakeview' (not --AWH) -> recommend 'lakefront', measured at the high-water line as the curation doc requires. CDEC's highest reservoir elevation 2016-2026 is 472.5 ft (May 2024/2025), ~144.9 m NAVD88. On 3DEP the ground falls to that level 3-7 m from sites 49 (39.816895,-122.369919; pad 145.8 m), 50 (39.817074,-122.370115; 145.8 m) and 51 (39.817180,-122.370140; 145.6 m), and ~15 m from 37 (39.814705,-122.367743; 146.7 m). In each case the pad sits ~1-1.8 m above the full-pool edge over a gentle bank (about 10-17%). Imagery shows the bare drawdown zone running up to those pads, with only scattered trees and no road between. All of them are reservable by the night on recreation.gov (RV/Tent/Trailer, posted lengths 100/57/47/20 ft). Site 38 (39.815202,-122.368211) is ~2.8 m above over ~13 m, which is borderline. Caveat: the water reaches this edge only in spring. CDEC read 443.9 ft in September 2026 (~9 m lower), when the shore is a long walk across bare lakebed. Proposed evidence: 'rec.gov catalog points + 3DEP + CDEC BLB 2026-11-27: high water 472.5 ft (~144.9 m NAVD88); pads 49/50/51 at 145.6-145.8 m, ground reaches high water 3-7 m out; 37 at 146.7 m, ~15 m; bare drawdown zone runs to the pads on imagery, scattered trees, no road; seasonal - drawn down ~9 m by September.'
